all.altText: 6 to 10 Day Precipitation Outlook issued September 1, 2026, valid September 7 to 11, 2026. A 50 to 60 percent chance of above-normal precipitation covers much of the interior West, including eastern California, the Northern and Central Great Basin, the Southwest, and parts of the Northern and Central Rockies. A 40 to 50 percent chance of above-normal precipitation spans parts of the Pacific Northwest, California, Southwest, and Northern and Central Plains. A broad area of 33 to 40 percent chance of above-normal precipitation covers much of the western and central United States.

8 to 14 Day Precipitation Outlook issued September 1, 2026, valid September 9 to 15, 2026. A broad area of 33 to 40 percent chance of above-normal precipitation covers much of the western United States, excepting the Olympic Peninsula in the Northwest Pacific region, which is forecast to have near-normal precipitation. 40 to 50 percent chance of above-normal precipitation stretches from the Southwest northward through the Central and Northern Great Basin into parts of the Northern Rockies. A 50 to 60 percent chance of above-normal precipitation covers southern California and southwestern Arizona.

all.altText:
Dangerous heat will persist across the Southwest through Friday with daytime highs of 110-115°F. Expect numerous daily record highs and Major to Extreme HeatRisk. Little overnight relief is expected as many areas may not cool below 80°F for several nights in a row. Temperatures return to near-normal levels over the weekend.
Dangerous heat will build across the Southern Plains again beginning this weekend, and persist into next week. Daytime highs of 95-105°F, with limited recovery at night due to lows only in the mid-70s (°F), will result in widespread Major to Extreme HeatRisk.
Increased chances for extreme heat continue into early Sep. A moderate risk (40-60% chance) of extreme heat remains highlighted across the south-central CONUS and Lower and Middle Mississippi, and Tennessee Valleys, Sep 4-6.
Limit outdoor activity, stay hydrated, and ensure access to A/C or cooling centers. Check on vulnerable family, friends, and neighbors. Never leave kids or pets unattended in vehicles.

More than a 60 percent chance of tropical cyclone development is indicated for the East Pacific from August 26 to September 1; with a 40 to 60 percent chance closer to the Central Pacific. From September 2-8, a 20 to 60 percent chance of tropical cyclone development is designated for the East and Central Pacific. This product is updated once per week and targets broad scale conditions integrated over a 7-day period for US interests only. This graphic does not indicate track or potential landfall of tropical systems. Refer to the National Hurricane Center (NHC) at www.nhc.noaa.gov.
